links.reason: குடையொடு கோல்வீழ (line 2) in the queen's dream is answered word for word by தாழ்ந்த குடையன் தளர்ந்தசெங் கோலன் (line 83) at the verdict. The omen precedes and the fulfilment follows the breaking of the anklet, so the pair shows the fall decided before the proof.

Both decades turn from the camp to waiting women: பாயல் உய்யுமோ (16.14) and the women who draw days on the wall, நெடும்சுவர் நாள்பல எழுதி (68.17). The warriors' own longing (பல்உறை பெறுபகொல், 68.14) is set beside them, as the note says. But two poems do not make 'a set part of Chera praise', and the அரிவையர் bound to the king's chest (68.19) are not plainly 'the whole palace'.

The herd girls will bind the gored wounds to their breasts (முலை வேதின் ஒற்றி முயங்கிப் பொதிவேம், 106.35) and take the tamer's blood as an ornament, and the poem itself likens the bulls to warriors entering battle (களம் புகும் மள்ளர், 106.9-10). The mother of 278 rejoices at சிதைந்துவே றாகிய படுமகன். Both read the wound as proof of worth, and both put a woman's breast against it (முலைஅறுத் திடுவென் in 278), so the move from mother to beloved is real.

The friend's reassurance from omens and season is shared: பல்லியும் பாங்கில் தேற்றும் and the season question in Natrinai 246, ஐயந்தீர் காட்சி and வலம் in Kar Narpathu 12. But Natrinai 246 never says 'right': its lizard sounds இடூஉ ஊங்கண் (perhaps on the left), so 'the right side being lucky in both' is false. The claim that this is 'why' the poem ends in a question is unsupported.

Kuruntokai 1 makes the kanthal of சேஎய் குன்றம் red as blood (குருதிப் பூவின் குலைக்காந்தள்) after the field ran red (செங்களம்). Paripadal 18.35-36 likens the close kanthal to the hands of men bound after defeat (போர் தோற்றுக் கட்டுண்டார் கை போல்வ). Both are war readings of one flower of Murugan's hill, one by colour and one by shape, as the teaches says.

Kural 1131 calls the madal ஏமம் and வலி; Kuruntokai 32 calls riding it பழி, but living apart is equally பழி (வாழ்தலும் பழியே), so it too leaves the madal as the lover's remaining course. Shameful and still the only strength are not incompatible claims, and the Kural's own chapter admits the shame. The Kuruntokai adds the dishonour as a condition, so qualifies fits, not tension.

Natrinai 202 likens the kongam to the lamps of the Karthigai month (அறுமீன் பயந்த அறம் செய் திங்கள் செல் சுடர்). Akananuru 17 likens falling silk-cotton flowers to the lamps of a festival town (விழவுத் தலைக்கொண்ட பழவிறல் மூதூர் நெய்உமிழ் சுடரின்). One distinctive image of the paalai road is spoken by the eloping man, who offers it, and by the foster mother, whose road is நீர்இல் அத்தத்து ஆர்இடை, so the shift by speaker is true.

Kural 13 has hunger torment the whole world when விண் பொய்ப்பின். Pattinappalai has வான்பொய்ப்பினும் தான்பொய்யா கடற்காவிரி. On the literal reading the delta is the exception that the Kural's rule does not allow, and the note names that reading. மலைத்தலைய (line 6) does give the river a source in the hills, though 'begins as rain' adds to it a little.

Ainkurunuru 105 says the brow is பொன்னினும் சிவந்தன்று since the lord வந்தென. The word may be the glow of joy at his coming (the marker flags it), and the link needs it to be pallor. Akananuru 156's friend speaks to the man, not the mother (தலைமகனை வரைவு கடாயது), so the claim that one poem's 'disclosure is the answer' to the other's rite is built across two unrelated settings.

Both mock the diviner with நன்று: in Natrinai 282 it is the unreal wish கிளவியின் தணியின் நன்றுமன் (would that his word could ease it), and in Ainkurunuru 248 it is நன்றால் அம்ம நின்றஇவள் நலனே, said if the வேலன் is to learn the cause by his கழங்கு. The first aims at the cure and the second at the reading of the beads, so the teaches holds.

Kural 1248 calls the following heart பேதை. Natrinai 107 calls the heart that went with him நல்வினைப்பாற்றே and herself, left in ஆனாக் கௌவை, நோய்ப்பாலேனே. These are opposite verdicts on the same heart that follows the man, and the gossip is the stated reason she envies it. Her laughter (நகுவேன்) is bitter, but the valuation still differs.

The formula is real: புன் தலை மந்தி வன்பறழ் ... நன்மலை நாட ... நின் நயந்து உறைவி in both. Natrinai 168 forbids the night visit and Ainkurunuru 273 his leaving (நீசெலின் ... கலிழ்மே). The shared formula is the substance, so same_image fits better than qualifies. 'Her life is staked' holds only for Natrinai 168 (இன் உயிர்); Ainkurunuru 273 speaks of tears, and marriage is the reader's inference.

Both make the woman a medicine: மருந்து எனப்படூஉம் மடவோள் (Natrinai 384.11) and தன்நோய்க்குத் தானே மருந்து (Kural 1102). But Natrinai 384 gives the man no reason for taking her across the waste; he bids his heart look at the vengai flowers spread for her to walk on. 'He now carries his medicine with him' as the reason for udanpokku is the proposer's.

The two poems share a frame: a flowering forest is seen and the man turns back (கானம் காணூஉ ... வந்தனர், 357; கானம் காணின் ... வந்தனர், 499). In 357 his own wish turns him (விரும்பி, அழுங்குக செய்பொருள் செலவு). In 499 it is the thought that she would grieve (வருந்துவள் பெரிதென). The second adds her suffering as the condition of return, so the type fits.

The mirage-chasing deer on a reported road (என்ப) is shared: மான் நசையுறூஉம் with ஏகுவர் என்ப in Natrinai 84, and அத்தமா ... நீர்என்று செத்து with என்பவால் in Kainnilai 24. But Natrinai 84's closing இரந்தோர் மாற்றல் ஆற்றா இல்லின் வாழ்க்கை வல்லாதோர் may be bitter rather than an excuse. A man who goes for duty and one who is நண்பிலார் are not incompatible, so tension is a stretch.

Both address a thing of nature about seeing the man: படாஅதி வாழி மதி in the Kural, and the hill that hid him (என்னையை மறைத்த குன்றே), blessed with அறஞ்சாலியரோ. But the Tamil does not fix that the blessing is a wish for his safety. என்னை may also be 'my father' (the marker notes this), so 'her wish can only be for what the hill will do to him' overstates.

Akananuru 170 makes the crab the only possible messenger (ஒருநின் அல்லது பிறிதுயாதும் இலனே; நீயே சொல்லல் வேண்டுமால் அலவ). Natrinai 277 sends the bee (என் நிலை உரையாய் சென்று) after reproaching it for sucking the yellow peeram while passing over her equally yellow pallor (பசலை ஊதாய்). The complaint against the messenger is specific to Natrinai 277, as the teaches says.

Both have the bangles register his leaving (Kural 1277 தணந்தமை ... உணர்ந்த வளை; Ainkurunuru 192 பிரிந்தென நெகிழ்ந்தன). The added point rests on வீங்கின meaning the bangles grew tight again at his return, and the marker flags that sense as uncertain. The Kural's point is that the bangles knew before she did (நம்மினும் முன்னம்), which the teaches passes over.

The evening shares her grief in both: புன்கண்ணை வாழி மருள்மாலை in the Kural, and வானமும் நம்மே போலும் மம்மர்த்து in Kuruntokai 310. Kuruntokai 310 does end on a wish for a messenger (உரைக்குநர்ப் பெறினே). But one poem cannot show that 'the evening lament is the point where the heroine starts to seek a go-between'; that is a generalisation.

Kuruntokai 25's only witness is a heron intent on fish (குருகும் உண்டு தான் மணந்த ஞான்றே), and the girl is helpless if he lies (தான் அது பொய்ப்பின் யான் எவன் செய்கோ). Thinaimalai 37 makes the tide the witness of that day (ஓதநீர் அன்றறியும்) and asks for marriage மன்றறிய. The mute witness against the public square is a specific connection.

Kural 1168's night has put all creatures to sleep (மன்னுயிர் எல்லாம் துயிற்றி) and has only her as companion. Natrinai 348 wakes moon, festival town (விழவு அயரும்) and paired bees (தாம் அமர் துணையொடு) around her sleeplessness (கண்படை இலெனே) and asks என்னொடு பொரும்கொல் இவ் உலகம். The contrast between a sleeping world and a revelling one is in the Tamil.

Natrinai 156 refuses the night and names the day at the millet (பல் நாள் சிறு தினை காக்குவம் ... பகல் வந்தீமோ). Akananuru 118 closes the day by gossip (பகல்வரின் கவ்வை அஞ்சுதும்) and the night by the tiger, and the girl has stopped the millet songs (கிளிகடி பாடலும் ஒழிந்தனள்). The colophon says இரவும் பகலும் வாரல் with வரைவு. The millet as the deciding place is in both poems.

The reversal is real: in Purananuru 107 Pari's only rival is the rain (மாரியும் உண்டு), and in Paripadal 22.7-8 the sky pours like the king's bounty (அவன் வண்மைபோல் வானம் பொழிந்த நீர்). But Kapilar does not 'let the rain win': the denial of Pari's uniqueness is itself the praise, and it grants him equality with the rain. Paripadal 22.10-15 is broken.
links.text_issue: Paripadal 22 lines 10, 12, 14, 15 have lacunae and line 13 is garbled.

links.reason: The formula is the same words: மன்னா உலகத்து மன்னுதல் குறித்தோர் தம்புகழ் நிறீஇ (Purananuru 165.1-2), and நயம் புரிந்து இன்னது செய்தாள் இவள் என மன்னா உலகத்து மன்னுவது புரைமே (Kalittokai 54.18-20). The heroine claims for an act of love the lasting fame the puram formula gives to givers. Lines 16-17 are compressed, but the borrowing does not depend on them.

The formula is shared: உளையணிந்து ... கலிமாவும் பூட்டிய (Kar 22) and உளையார் கலிநன் மாப்பூட்டி வருவார் (Kainnilai 33). These are separate poems by different poets, so the friend's words cannot show that her comfort is 'an accurate picture of what is happening on the road'. Kainnilai 33 has lost most of lines 1-2, which leaves its speaker partly guessed.

The echo is closer than the note says: Ainthinai Aimpathu 25 has both குழல் (as the boy's tuft) and மழலைவாய், the two key words of Kural 66 (குழல் இனிது ... மழலைச்சொல்). But its sentence leaves the verb unsaid (the marker flags this), so 'eases the pain of longing' is supplied. The rule-and-instance teaches is plausible but rests on that supplied verb.

Both read the red thonri as flame: தலைநாள் விளக்கிற் றகையுடைய (Kar 26) and பொருதீ என வெருளும் (Kainnilai 26). But in Kainnilai 26 the fright belongs to a creature in the scene, or possibly to the addressee, and line 2 is broken. The friend's message stays certainty (அரிது அவர் வாரா விடல்), so 'a trace of fear in her comfort' is not shown.

The image is real and distinctive: a பறைதபு heron at Thondi in both (பறைதபு நாரை ... தொண்டி முன்றுறை; பறைதபு முதுகுருகு ... தொண்டி). But in Ainkurunuru 180 the fed heron is only part of Thondi, to which the girl's beauty is likened. Reading it as the dependent girl the man must provide for, and as an 'answer' to Paranar's poem, is not fixed by the Tamil, and the marker declined to tag it.

Evening music is shared: தீங்குழல் ஆம்பலின் இனிய இமிரும் (the bee, Ainkurunuru 215) and ஆயன் குழல் ... கொல்லும் படை (Kural 1228). But Ainkurunuru 215 does not say the music wounds her. It says those who part at such an evening will do worse (இதனினும் கொடிய செய்குவர்). The Kural's flute is itself sweet music turned deadly, so the contrast between harshness and sweetness is false.

Both have the mother forbid the ford because of a chariot: பல்கால் வரூஉம் தேரென செல்லாதீமோ (Ainkurunuru 186), and கொடிதுஅறி பெண்டிர் சொற்கொண்டு அன்னை கடிகொண்டனளே ... தேர் உண்டு எனவே (Akananuru 20). Ainkurunuru 186 does not say the mother saw the chariot herself, so the 'two strengths' of the teaches, report against sight, is unsupported.

Kural 969 (the noble give up life when honour is at stake, மானம் வரின்) and Kural 1080 (the base sell themselves when trouble comes, ஒன்று உற்றக்கால்) describe two kinds of people. They make no incompatible claims, so this is a contrast, not a tension. 'The book ends on the second' is a fact about placement, not something the pairing teaches.

The puram name is a real link: கொங்கு புறம் பெற்ற கொற்ற வேந்தே (Purananuru 373.8) and புனனாடன் கொங்கரை அட்ட களத்து (Kalavazhi Narpathu 14). But every Kalavazhi stanza ends on களத்து by the work's form, so ending 'on the field itself' is not Poigaiyar's choice for this victory. The two may also be different kings. Purananuru 373 is badly broken.

Ainkurunuru 59's friend was once the medicine (நினக்குமருந்தாகிய யான்) and is now none for the wife (இவட்குமருந்து அன்மை). Kural 1102 makes the beloved herself the only cure (தன்நோய்க்குத் தானே மருந்து). The pair limits the couplet: the cure ran through a third person and does not run back to the woman.

Kural 1187 has the pallor come the instant she turns from his embrace (புடைபெயர்ந்தேன் அவ்வளவில்). Natrinai 304 makes the same exchange a rule: புணரின் புணருமார் எழிலே பிரியின் ... சிதைக்குமார் பசலை. It then sums it in the chest that holds இன்பமும் துன்பமும் like the hands of asunam-killers, which is a development beyond the couplet's single moment.

Natrinai 226's maxim வளம் கெடப் பொன்னும் கொள்ளார் மன்னர் is the counsel of Purananuru 184, where a king who takes by measure (நெறியறிந்து கொளினே) keeps the land rich and a grasping one is யானை புக்க புலம். The wife turns the maxim on a husband who goes for wealth not knowing its measure (செய்பொருள் அளவு அறியார), herself being the source (நாம் தம் உண்மையின் உளமே).

Water as medicine and as a sign of the lover's land is shared: விருந்தின் தீம் நீர் மருந்தும் ஆகும் (Natrinai 53), and அவர்நாட்டு ... கலிழி நீரே sweeter than தேன்மயங்கு பாலினும் (Ainkurunuru 203). But Natrinai 53 explicitly leaves open whether the mother knows (அறிந்தனள்கொல்லோ அருளினள்கொல்லோ), so 'without knowing whose hill it is' contradicts it. Nor does it say the hill is his.

Patitruppattu 72 blames the foes' folly: சூழாது துணிதல் and நின் பண்புநன்கு அறியார் மடம்பெருமையின். Patitruppattu 84 says they knew his strength well (வலியை ஆதல்நற்கு அறிந்தனர் ஆயினும்) and still rose because they did not know how to bow (வணங்கல் அறியார்). The move from ignorance to pride is in the Tamil.

The situations match: செய்த குறியும் பொய்யாயின ... ஐயகொல் ஆன்றார் தொடர்பு (Thinaimozhi 41), and the friend in Natrinai 11 who tells the heroine, wilting since அவர் செய் குறி பிழைப்ப, to drop the thought வாரார். But the two poems are not one exchange. Natrinai 11 offers the chariot's arrival as proof, not his 'gentleness' (sparing the crab is the marker's suggestion), and its colophon puts the failure down to guarding.

Kural 957 says a fault in the well-born shows like the spot on the moon (மதிக்கண் மறுப்போல்). Kalittokai 41.23-24 says a falsehood in his truth would be fire in the moon (திங்களுள் தீத் தோன்றியற்று), an impossibility. It is sung so that the hidden man hears (மறை நின்று கேட்டு அருளி, 41.41). The same figure is turned from a warning into a pledge.

The mother asks என்னும் உள்ளினள் கொல்லோ (Ainkurunuru 372), and the other mother states தற்புரந்து எடுத்த எற்றுந்து உள்ளாள் (Akananuru 383), both amid gossip (அலரெழ in both). The doubt and the charge are on the same point, whether the girl thinks of her mother, so the pairing is specific.

The materialist dismisses knowledge of a former birth as the delusion of possession or dream (தெய்வ மயக்கினும் கனா உறு திறத்தினும் ... ஐயம் அன்றி இல்லை). In kaathai 9 Manimekalai knows her former birth without error (பிறப்பு வழு இன்று உணர்ந்து; மயக்கு அற உணர்ந்தேன்). The clash of மயக்கு against மயக்கு அற makes the tension real. The speakers of 27.278-283 are inferred.

Three of the four terms match: தன்நிலை and தன்வலி, தொழில்நிலை and வினைவலி, துப்பெதிர்ந்தார் இல்நிலை and மாற்றான் வலி. The claimed shift rests on reading ஈடில் இயல்நிலை as 'the order of things', an uncertain gloss. The teaches turns on that reading.

Kar Narpathu 1 gives Mal the rainbow as his chest garland (பொருகடல் வண்ணன் புனைமார்பிற் றார்போல் திருவில்). Ainthinai Aimpathu 1 gives Mal the cloud's colour (மல்லர்க் கடந்தான் நிறம்போல்), Murugan the lightning and Shiva the konrai garland (எயில் எய்தவன் தார் பூப்ப). Each opening mullai verse shares the storm out among gods in its own way.

Both use அணங்கு: அணங்குகொல் in Kural 1081, and சுணங்கென நினைதி நீயே அணங்கென நினையும் in Ainkurunuru 363. But சுணங்கு on the breasts is a mark of beauty, and the poem does not say she thinks it a blemish. அணங்கு there may be the striking, afflicting power (அணங்குறு நெஞ்சே) rather than 'goddess'. The 'gap between how she sees herself' rests on that misreading.

iraicchi.act: the male tiger, raging, leaps on a tusker's face to end the hunger of his mate who has just given birth in the rock cave
iraicchi.sense: the man too has gone into danger to provide for her, so she accepts his journey (வருந்தேன் ... வாய்க்க அவர் செலவே)

poems.note: The colophon names the friend, but line 12 reads as the heroine's own words.
The neythal cut by the wheel is literal evidence of his visits; the thurai gives no situation for a hidden comparison.
The mango shoot is openly compared (போல) with the Eyinar girl, so neither device applies.
The season that came when he did not is the poem's stated sense, not a sense rising from a carrier.
The fish = the man who takes what drops to him, and the ripe fruit falling from the field mango = the parattai who came to him unasked; the open simile ஆடிப் பாவை போல is separate.
Prawn = the girl; heron's catch escaped = the danger already survived; the white thazhai bud it fears = the report that he has left.
The foolish peacocks are named openly as mistaken (மடவ) and are a flock joined by the pidavu, so condition 1 was hard to judge.

iraicchi.act: the long-legged kanandhul warns travellers of the bandits and turns them back
iraicchi.sense: the bird does what the women failed to do: had they spoken (சொல்லினமாயின்) he too might have been turned back from the journey for wealth

iraicchi.act: the tusker plucks the millet ears to relieve his mate, worn out after calving
iraicchi.sense: as the tusker ends his mate's distress, the man has come to marry and end the girl's suffering from the night visits (இரவின் வரூஉம் இடும்பை நாம் உய வரைய வந்த)

poems.note: A puram passage (வாகை); both fields are null by rule.

iraicchi.act: the old stag that escaped the tiger calls his doe in a male voice to come close
iraicchi.sense: the youth calls her daughter to keep beside him on the waste, as the stag guards his doe

poems.note: The tender pair sits inside the mother's curse, so the sense runs against her stated grief.
Lines 4-5 are hard to construe, so no sense of the leap could be stated.
The bee leaving the kanthal is joined to the man by the comparative -இன், so it is an open comparison.
